analysis:
Examined the three changed files. The PR adds two metadata fields, `serving` (a ClusterServedScope enum) and `tensorAssistant` (a Bool?), to the cluster served-speed records and pair telemetry. It also adds a `Setup.servedAs` filter and extends the retention key in ClusterServedSpeedFile.adding (ClusterPairTelemetry.swift head ~197-198). These are planning and routing performance metadata, kept in owner-only local files under ~/.darkbloom/cluster. None are in the coordinator-provider wire protocol, attestation, encryption, or billing paths.

Data exposure: the new fields are an enum and a bool, with no prompt, token, or client identity, so the existing 'values only' posture holds (A-001 unaffected). Input validation: `Setup.servedAs` and `servedBy` are pure filters. `ClusterServedSpeedRecords.add` and `decode` keep their size bounds (1 MiB cap; field length and build-hash checks). The new enum Codable decode rejects unknown strings and throws a decode error. Callers of the served-speed read path handle failure by returning nil or throwing; ClusterServedSpeedFile.read already uses `try?`, so malformed data fails closed to no records.

Availability: a record with a nil `serving` is read as matching any scope, but `servedBy` still excludes records with no build hashes. The `tensorAssistant == true` guard in `measurements(entries:...)` skips such setups and appends a line. No new crash paths were seen; `Int(...)` conversions and divisions are unchanged from base.

Residual integration questions: the callers that populate `serving` and `tensorAssistant` (leader telemetry writer, planner, router) and `ClusterServedModes.figures` are not in the supplied evidence. The ClusterPairTelemetry.swift base lines (e.g. 188) are not changed in a security-relevant way. A local same-UID process could already tamper with served-speed.json (pre-existing, steering only plans), and this PR does not change that. No threat-model regression was identified.
